title: Mina's Bee-dazzled Cake
markdown:
The air in Sunny Meadow was thick with the sweet smell of summer. Ripe strawberries and golden sugar tickled everyone’s noses. It was the most exciting day of the year for many garden friends: the Great Garden Bake-Off. Under a big bright tent, happy whispers filled the air. Little Mina the mouse, whiskers wiggling with excitement, smoothed down her brand-new clean apron. Today was her day. Today she would win the special blue ribbon. Mina loved to bake more than anything. For many weeks she had dreamed and planned. She was making her special cake: a big three-layered honey cake, covered in the fluffiest smoothest frosting, then decorated with tiny sparkly edible pearls. She imagined it the most perfect, the most elegant, and the most delicious cake ever.

High on a strong branch of the old oak that watched over the tent sat Rowan the rook. Rowan was not very good at making cakes. He liked shiny things more than sticky frosting. What he could not bake, he made up for by watching. From his leafy spot he saw everything: busy ants putting out currant buns; Mrs Rabbit, proud, fussing over her prize carrot cake.

“All this fuss over a few crumbs and a bit of jam,” Rowan cawed to himself, a playful glint in his beady eyes.

Just then a familiar cozy presence arrived. Gran Elin, a wonderfully plump badger with glasses on her nose and a little flour on her apron, ambled over. Her presence felt like a warm hug on a cool day.

“Are you ready for your moment, little star?” she asked, voice as soft as a favourite armchair. Gran Elin was famous through Sunny Meadow for warm hugs and a calm kind voice.

“Almost, Gran,” Mina squeaked. Her tiny paws trembled as she placed the last dewdrop pearl. “It just needs to be perfectly neat.” She had spent hours drawing perfect lines of frosting around the edges of the top layer. She wanted the cake to show how tidy she could be.

The judges, a wise group of hedgehogs and a rather particular ladybug named Mrs Higgins, began. They tiptoed through the tent, tasting. Cakes dotted with juicy berries, sweet and tart. Cakes piled with whipped cream like clouds. Cakes with frosting flowers too pretty to eat. Finally they came to Mina’s table. They stopped. They leaned in. The cake was a sight: perfectly neat, swirls so even they looked drawn with an invisible ruler.

Bartholomew Hedgehog, the head judge, looked even closer. He squinted. Then he straightened, a funny look spreading across his whiskered face. He let out a soft surprised snort. Mrs Higgins let out a little giggle. Soon quiet laughing spread through the watching crowd. Not loud booming laughter. A gentle happy giggling that filled the tent with warmth.

Mina’s tiny ears bent down. Oh dear. Had she done something wrong? Her cake was so neat. She had not made a single wobbly swirl.

From his high branch, Rowan let out a happy caw. He had seen something funny earlier, something no one else had noticed in the busy baking. As Mina was so carefully drawing her perfect swirls, a very big fuzzy bumblebee had been taking a nap on a nearby rose bush. The gentle whirring of the tent fans had woken it. With a sleepy stretch and a big yawn, the bee uncurled. Then, in a moment of pure sleepy silliness, it tumbled. Right onto Mina’s cake.

Amazingly, the landing had not made the frosting messy. But as the bee buzzed away, its fuzzy body and plump pollen-dusted legs had left a perfectly round, slightly flattened shape right in the middle of Mina’s neat swirls. To the amused garden folk, it looked exactly as if a very surprised, very fuzzy bee had decided to take a short nap on the cake.

Mina followed everyone’s gaze. She saw the funny fuzzy mark. She had been so busy thinking about perfect neatness, she had not even seen her unexpected visitor.

A tiny shy smile began to spread. Then she heard Gran Elin’s gentle warm chuckle beside her. Rowan from his tree let out another happy caw.

The importance of being perfectly neat loosened its hold. The little bee-shaped dent, made completely by accident, made the cake look wonderfully alive. A little bit funny. The laughter was not mean. Everyone was laughing with Mina, sharing the joke.

She looked at her cake, then at Gran, then at Rowan, bright eyes twinkling in the sun. A lovely warmth spread through her, even sweeter than honey cake. She had not won the blue ribbon for the most elegant cake. Quite surprisingly, she had made the funniest, most memorable cake in the whole Bake-Off. Around her the tent hummed with friends and family, and the bee-shaped dent sat in the frosting like a guest who had been invited after all.
characters: Mina (a neat honey-cake mouse), Rowan (a shiny-thing-watching rook), Gran Elin (a flour-aproned badger)
author: StoryGen Community
